developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/* — literal facts as of 2026-10-01
Public beta since 2026-09-10.
Session create: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions   header: OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1
Concepts: Agent (model, instructions, tools, MCP servers) | Environment (optional sandbox) | Session (durable agent instance) | Events/items
Managed harness tools: programmatic tool calling, MCP server connections (HTTP transport), web search, code execution in sandbox, file editing, command execution
Subagents: delegation supported; up to 4 concurrent subagents in documented examples
OpenAI manages: sessions, orchestration, context compaction, recovery. Application provides tools and chooses execution environment.
"The Agents API retains session state so you can continue work across turns without rebuilding the conversation context."
Data residency: United States only.
Zero Data Retention (ZDR): NOT SUPPORTED, even with self-hosted sandboxes.

COMPUTER USE TOOL (added 2026-09-29):
 tool type "computer_use", environment "openai_hosted" — browser runs in an OpenAI-controlled environment.
 Origin approval: computer_use_approval_request, type browser_origin_access, raised once per NEW ORIGIN incl. public sites.
   Docs: origin approval "does not enforce confirmation before individual actions".
   Mitigation OpenAI suggests: restrict the browser to safe resources, or use a locally-controlled runtime.
 Authentication: browser_authentication approval request. App renders login choices + fields, collects email / password /
   verification codes, submits via the SESSION EVENTS ENDPOINT using field IDs and values.
   "Never pass credentials in ordinary messages" — only through dedicated authentication events.
   Supported: email addresses, passwords, verification codes. NOT supported: passkeys, QR-code sign-in.
 Screenshots: optional; may contain sensitive page/account data; OpenAI says keep them out of application logs.
 App controls: session create/delete, task instructions, browser behavior, origin + auth approvals, credential collection,
   screenshot display/retention.
